§29.17(i) Second Solution

ⓘ
Keywords:
Lamé’s equation, second solution
Permalink:
http://dlmf.nist.gov/29.17.i
See also:
Annotations for §29.17 and Ch.29

If (29.2.1) admits a Lamé polynomial solution E, then a second linearly independent solution F is given by

29.17.1 F⁡(z)=E⁡(z)⁢∫i⁢K′⁡zdu(E⁡(u))2.
ⓘ
Symbols:
K′⁡(k): Legendre’s complementary complete elliptic integral of the first kind, dx: differential of x, i: imaginary unit, ∫: integral, z: complex variable and k: real parameter
Permalink:
http://dlmf.nist.gov/29.17.E1
Encodings:
TeX, pMML, png
See also:
Annotations for §29.17(i), §29.17 and Ch.29

For properties of these solutions see Arscott (1964b, §9.7), Erdélyi et al. (1955, §15.5.1), Shail (1980), and Sleeman (1966b).

§29.17(ii) Algebraic Lamé Functions

ⓘ
Keywords:
Lamé functions, algebraic, algebraic Lamé functions
Permalink:
http://dlmf.nist.gov/29.17.ii
See also:
Annotations for §29.17 and Ch.29

Algebraic Lamé functions are solutions of (29.2.1) when ν is half an odd integer. They are algebraic functions of sn⁡(z,k), cn⁡(z,k), and dn⁡(z,k), and have primitive period 8⁢K⁡. See Erdélyi (1941c), Ince (1940b), and Lambe (1952).

§29.17(iii) Lamé–Wangerin Functions

ⓘ
Keywords:
Lamé–Wangerin functions
Permalink:
http://dlmf.nist.gov/29.17.iii
See also:
Annotations for §29.17 and Ch.29

Lamé–Wangerin functions are solutions of (29.2.1) with the property that (sn⁡(z,k))1/2⁢w⁡(z) is bounded on the line segment from i⁢K′⁡ to 2⁢K⁡+i⁢K′⁡. See Erdélyi et al. (1955, §15.6).
